examples/readonly-cmdsub.sh.stdout:
============================================================
 SECTION 1: Basic readonly variable
============================================================
--- [01-readonly-var] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        readonly MY_VAR="hello_world"
        echo "MY_VAR=${MY_VAR}"
        # Attempt to change it (will fail, but we capture)
        MY_VAR="changed" 2>/dev/null || echo "Assignment denied: $?"
        echo "MY_VAR after attempted change=${MY_VAR}"
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : MY_VAR=hello_world
MY_VAR after attempted change=hello_world
  stderr  : bash: line 5: MY_VAR: readonly variable

============================================================
 SECTION 2: readonly -p  (print readonly variables)
============================================================
--- [02-readonly-p] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        readonly FOO=alpha
        readonly BAR=beta
        readonly -p | head -5
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : declare -r BAR="beta"
declare -r BASHOPTS="checkwinsize:cmdhist:complete_fullquote:extquote:force_fignore:globasciiranges:globskipdots:hostcomplete:interactive_comments:patsub_replacement:progcomp:promptvars:sourcepath"
declare -ar BASH_VERSINFO=([0]="5" [1]="2" [2]="21" [3]="1" [4]="release" [5]="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu")
declare -ir EUID="1008"
declare -r FOO="alpha"

============================================================
 SECTION 3: readonly -f  (readonly functions)
============================================================
--- [03-readonly-f] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        myfunc() { echo "Hello from myfunc"; }
        readonly -f myfunc
        myfunc
        # Attempt to unset the function (will fail)
        unset -f myfunc 2>/dev/null || echo "unset -f denied"
        # Verify function still exists
        myfunc
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : Hello from myfunc
unset -f denied
Hello from myfunc

============================================================
 SECTION 4: readonly -a  (indexed array)
============================================================
--- [04-readonly-a] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        declare -a MY_ARR=(zero one two)
        readonly -a MY_ARR
        echo "MY_ARR[0]=${MY_ARR[0]}"
        echo "MY_ARR[1]=${MY_ARR[1]}"
        # Attempt to change an element (will fail)
        MY_ARR[0]=ZERO 2>/dev/null || echo "Array assignment denied"
        echo "MY_ARR[0] after attempt=${MY_ARR[0]}"
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : MY_ARR[0]=zero
MY_ARR[1]=one
MY_ARR[0] after attempt=zero
  stderr  : bash: line 7: MY_ARR: readonly variable

============================================================
 SECTION 5: readonly -A  (associative array)
============================================================
--- [05-readonly-A] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        declare -A MY_ASSOC=([key1]=val1 [key2]=val2)
        readonly -A MY_ASSOC
        echo "MY_ASSOC[key1]=${MY_ASSOC[key1]}"
        echo "MY_ASSOC[key2]=${MY_ASSOC[key2]}"
        # Attempt to change (will fail)
        MY_ASSOC[key1]=CHANGED 2>/dev/null || echo "Assoc assignment denied"
        echo "MY_ASSOC[key1] after attempt=${MY_ASSOC[key1]}"
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : MY_ASSOC[key1]=val1
MY_ASSOC[key2]=val2
MY_ASSOC[key1] after attempt=val1
  stderr  : bash: line 7: MY_ASSOC: readonly variable

============================================================
 SECTION 6: readonly --  (no more options)
============================================================
--- [06a-readonly-dash-ok] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        readonly -- MYVAR=hello
        echo "MYVAR=${MYVAR}"
        # Confirm it is indeed readonly
        MYVAR=world 2>/dev/null || echo "Assignment denied (expected)"
    
  exitcode: 1
  stdout  : MYVAR=hello
  stderr  : bash: line 5: MYVAR: readonly variable

--- [06b-readonly-dash-invalid] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        readonly -- -notvalid 2>&1 || true
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : bash: line 2: readonly: `-notvalid': not a valid identifier

============================================================
 SECTION 7: Invalid variable name (error case)
============================================================
--- [07-invalid-name] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        readonly 123invalid 2>&1 || true
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : bash: line 2: readonly: `123invalid': not a valid identifier

============================================================
 SECTION 8: readonly -f -p  (list readonly functions)
============================================================
--- [08-readonly-f-p] ---
  cmd     : bash -c 
        f1() { :; }
        f2() { :; }
        readonly -f f1 f2
        readonly -f -p | head -5
    
  exitcode: 0
  stdout  : f1 () 
{ 
    :
}
